content:
sam_dev: Running into an SSL verify error on Windows CI when talking to Dedicated behind our corp proxy with a custom CA. Same setup works on mac/linux. Suspect SDK env var handling + client caching issue. Anyone seen this pattern?

jenna: Can you paste the error and a minimal repro?

sam_dev: Traceback from Windows runner:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:xxxx)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

httpx.ConnectError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='dedicated.redwood.example', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/ (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError("...")))
```
Minimal snippet we use (SDK 0.9.3):
```
import os
from redwood import AsyncClient

os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'] = 'https://dedicated.redwood.example'
os.environ['REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE'] = r'C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\custom-ca.pem'

client = AsyncClient(token='x', base_url=os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'])
await client.chat.completions.create(model='x', input='hi')
```
Locally and on our linux/mac runners the same file path works. Only Windows CI fails and looks like the SDK ended up using the system store or an older CA file.

mike_infra: Two hypotheses: (1) path normalization/backslash handling: we call Path(ca).resolve() then str() which on Windows might return backslashes or a UNC-ish path that httpx/ssl interprets differently; maybe convert to posix path. (2) client reuse: we cache AsyncClient instances keyed by process and base_url; if REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE was set earlier in the job and then overwritten by REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE later, a cached client could retain the earlier trust config.

olga: Also check which env var the SDK ends up honoring. We have REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE, plus we proxy through requests/httpx which look at SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. If the runner sets REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE early and we only read REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE later, mismatch is possible.

sam_dev: That matches my CI job: an earlier step sets REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to a CI-wide bundle, then later the job copies the Dedicated CA and sets REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE. Locally I only set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE so I didn't catch it.

jenna: As a workaround can you pass the CA directly into AsyncClient and disable env-trust? e.g.
```
client = AsyncClient(token='x', base_url=..., trust_env=False, ca=r'C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\custom-ca.pem')
```
Assuming the SDK forwards `ca`/`trust_env` to httpx.AsyncClient.

sam_dev: That fixed the job when I tried it. However, the current type stubs for AsyncClient in 0.9.3 don't include `ca` or `trust_env` in the constructor signature, so mypy complains.

mike_infra: Actionable plan: (A) normalize path handling when we convert env CA paths: Path(...).expanduser().resolve() -> as_posix() replacement to avoid backslash problems; (B) stop reusing AsyncClient across differing TLS configs: include (base_url, ca_path_normalized, trust_env) in the client cache key or avoid caching entirely for AsyncClient; (C) audit env var precedence: explicit REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE should override REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE; if both exist, log a warning. I'll draft a PR.

olga: Add a Windows CI integration reproducer: set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE first, then later overwrite REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE in the same job and run a small async call. We currently only run Dedicated e2e on linux/mac.

sam_dev: Also please update the typing: AsyncClient __init__ should accept `ca: Optional[Union[str, bytes, os.PathLike]] = None` and `trust_env: bool = True` so users passing them don't hit mypy errors. We should also document env var precedence in the devex guide.

mike_infra: Will include stub updates + docs + integration test. I'll reference issue #4721 and aim for a small unit test for path normalization and an integration Windows CI job.

deploy-bot: CI job redwood-sdk-windows-proxy reproduced the original failure (build/10112).

jenna: OK. Sam, once the PR lands can you validate against your Windows runner?

sam_dev: Yep, will validate and report back. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
